attributes.residual: 608/608 instructions, opcode multiset IDENTICAL (pure reorder), fuzzy 98.90625%, real 126, frame 0x120 - unchanged from the 2026-08-29 park. The ENTIRE residual is one instruction: the shared 0.0f pool load. Target issues it at 0x68, filling the load-use stall between `lwz r3,4(r30)` (0x64) and `lfs f0,112(r3)` (0x6c), into f1 - reusing f1 after the int-to-float magic double (loaded at 0x20) dies at 0x5c. Ours issues it at 0x28, filling the FIRST stall in the block (between `lwz r3,16(r30)` and `lwz r0,32(r3)`), which overlaps the magic's live range and therefore forces f2. Everything else is the downstream FPR recolor: blocks 2-4 come out register-swapped (target const=f0/field=f1, ours const=f1/field=f0) with identical opcodes at identical offsets. All 11 loads of this literal sit at the SAME 11 offsets in both streams; only the first one's position and color differ. ROOT CAUSE ESTABLISHED, three independent ways: (1) moving `f = 0.0f;` to the very top of the function produced a BYTE-IDENTICAL object with the lfs still at 0x28 - the placement is position-invariant, so it is not statement scheduling of that assignment; (2) grep of every branch target in the target disassembly shows NO branch lands anywhere in 0x28-0x68, so target and ours schedule the SAME single basic block - a basic-block-boundary explanation is ruled out; (3) the compare-form and declaration-order levers, which move register homes in other functions, were byte-neutral here. The choice is made inside MWCC's allocate-then-schedule pipeline (which FPR the first rematerialization of a repeatedly-used pool literal gets) and has no reachable source-level control. DO-NOT-RETRY on these axes: statement position, declaration order, compare-operand spelling, ternary/if-else polarity, extern-literal substitution.
